notes:
Background: small support SaaS aiming to augment agents with suggested replies and KB search. Signed up via docs, fast self-serve. Trial behavior: issued API key but minimal integration effort taken; initial PoC focused on full-context generation for agent assist (long tickets ~1.2k tokens). Observed bucket: low throughput, latency sensitivity for agent UX (<300ms target) but customer tolerates up to ~600ms for fallback.

Customer comments (paraphrase): 'We like Redwood performance claims but our engineering lead prefers vendor with prebuilt Zendesk plugin.' Also: 'Need SSO + audit logs for compliance later this year.' Pricing: SMB-sensitive, looking for clear per-message economics.

Technical notes: ran Redwood hosted endpoint, model used: small-open-v2 baseline; SE recommended prefix caching + reduce context window; customer didn't follow up on caching changes. Reported occasional 1.2s token latency spikes during PoC (sample logs attached in INF-4321).

Engagement summary: early-qualified inbound lead but trial stalled after API key issuance. Main risk vector: competitor switching because competitor already integrated into their stack and internal dev bandwidth constrained. Opportunity: provide targeted onboarding, integration code snippets for Zendesk, limited free credit and an expedited SE session to set up caching/batching.

Quoted lines from discovery call: "If you can show a Zendesk demo in 30m with realistic data, we'll prioritize integration work." — Engineering lead.

Internal next steps: 1) AE to rebook 20m technical demo (owner: Alex) 2) SE (Priya) to prepare Zendesk sample repo + 30-minute walkthrough 3) Offer $500 credit + 2-week extension to trial.
